title: Beyond Accumulation: The Intuitive Jump Model of Expert Decision Making in Sports
abstract: We propose the intuitive jump model of expert sport decisions, a dual-pathway conceptual framework in which an evidence accumulation route operates alongside a rapid, threshold-based intuitive route. Two studies with elite basketball athletes tested the hypothesis that time pressure induces a qualitative pathway shift rather than merely a boundary collapse. Study 1 ( N = 34) examined the model inputs, showing that trial-level cue informativeness ( C sensory ) from naturalistic videos reliably predicted faster correct responses, providing a behavioral proxy for accumulation efficiency. Using mid-range C sensory stimuli and a heuristic cue validity paradigm, Study 2 ( N = 30) contrasted no time pressure versus time pressure conditions. Analyses using an adapted process dissociation procedure revealed a selective dissociation: Time pressure selectively reduced the evidence accumulation contribution ( C ), whereas the intuitive jump contribution ( H ) remained statistically invariant. This dissociation provides behavioral evidence for the intuitive jump model’s jump mechanism and lays the behavioral groundwork for future mathematical formalizations.
